h: Play it clever, then see Reading's best bits
p: Reading's handy location makes it a brilliant meeting point for groups. Reading station is a major rail hub with fast trains from London and the west, and the Elizabeth line now runs right through to central London, so friends coming from different directions can all get there easily. From the station, King Street is just a short walk.

For your game, remember: search first, solve second. Many teams rush to crack the first padlock they see, when the clue they need is sitting in a drawer across the room. Gather everything you find, share it with the group, and look for links. Numbers on one object might match a symbol on another. Keep calm when the clock starts to bite, because panic is the enemy of good puzzling. And whatever happens, the post-game chat about who nearly cracked it is half the fun.

There's more to Reading than shopping. Reading Museum, in the Town Hall, is free to visit and home to a full-size Victorian replica of the Bayeux Tapestry, which is a real surprise for first-time visitors. Head north across the river to Caversham and you'll find Christchurch Meadows, a lovely green space beside the Thames with a playground and riverside paths. The Hexagon theatre hosts comedy, concerts and pantomime, and the town centre has plenty of restaurants for a celebratory meal. If you want to stretch your legs further, the Thames Path runs along the river and makes for a peaceful walk away from the bustle of the town.
